blocks: The Big Bang was not an explosion in space. It was the expansion of space itself.
Thirteen point eight billion years ago, everything we can see was packed into something smaller than an atom: unimaginably hot, unimaginably dense.
Then, in less than a trillionth of a trillionth of a trillionth of a second, space stretched faster than light. This is called inflation.
In the first three minutes, it cooled enough for protons and neutrons to fuse. Hydrogen and helium were born.
For three hundred eighty thousand years, the universe was a glowing fog. Then electrons joined the nuclei, and light flew free. We still detect it today, as the cosmic microwave background.
Gravity pulled the gas into clumps. A few hundred million years later, the first stars ignited, and galaxies grew along invisible filaments.
And we know it happened, because every distant galaxy is moving away from us. The universe is still expanding.
